description: Exhaustive blacklist of critical Android and OEM packages that must NEVER be uninstalled or disabled. Touching these packages causes bootloops, soft-bricks, broken telephony, or unusable system UI.

global.name: Android System
global.reason: Core Android OS framework and binder IPC backbone. Immediate kernel panic / bootloop.

global.name: System UI
global.reason: Renders status bar, quick settings, navigation, and lockscreen. Disabling drops phone into crash loop.

global.name: Phone Services
global.reason: Handles cellular radio, baseband RIL interface, and emergency calling. Total loss of cellular functionality.

global.name: Telephony Provider
global.reason: Database for SMS, MMS, APNs, and SIM card carrier profiles. Renders mobile data and SMS completely non-functional.

global.name: Telecom Server
global.reason: Audio routing for calls and emergency dialer management.

global.name: Settings
global.reason: System settings master activity and preferences provider. Disabling locks user out of device configuration.

global.name: Settings Intelligence
global.reason: Settings search index and preference provider on Android 10+.

global.name: Package Installer (AOSP)
global.reason: Manages APK installation, runtime permissions dialogs, and package validation.

global.name: Package Installer (Google)
global.reason: Modern Google package installer and permission controller. Disabling prevents any app installs or permission grants.

global.name: Permission Controller
global.reason: Android 10+ runtime permission engine. Disabling breaks all app permission checks and causes UI freezes.

global.name: Google Play Services
global.reason: Core Google services, SafetyNet, Play Integrity, FCM push notifications, location providers, and in-app billing.

global.name: Google Services Framework
global.reason: Handles communication between Google servers and Play Services. Removing breaks Google Account authentication.

global.name: Gboard
global.reason: Primary virtual keyboard on most Android builds. Disabling without another active IME locks user out upon password entry.

global.name: AOSP Keyboard
global.reason: Default fallback AOSP IME.

global.name: Microsoft SwiftKey
global.reason: Default keyboard on some OEM builds (e.g. Huawei/Samsung/Honor). Never remove if active keyboard.

global.name: Media Provider
global.reason: Indexes internal storage files, photos, audio, and documents. Disabling breaks file pickers and gallery.

global.name: Media Provider Mainline
global.reason: Project Mainline modular media framework. Disabling breaks storage access framework (SAF).

global.name: Download Manager
global.reason: Core Android download provider. Disabling halts browser downloads, Play Store updates, and OTA downloads.

global.name: Key Chain
global.reason: Stores cryptographic credentials and SSL certificates for system and banking applications.

global.name: Google Play Store
global.reason: Package installation, app updates and Play Integrity checks. Disabling it leaves the device without any way to install or update apps.

global.name: AOSP Launcher
global.reason: Fallback home screen on AOSP-style builds. Disabling without another launcher active leaves the device unnavigable.

global.name: AOSP Dialer
global.reason: Default phone UI on AOSP builds. Disabling removes the ability to place or answer calls.

xiaomi_hyperos.name: Xiaomi Security Center
xiaomi_hyperos.reason: CRITICAL: Hardcoded dependency across HyperOS/MIUI frameworks. Manages runtime security, IPC validation, and permission checks. Disabling causes an immediate 100% hard bootloop.

xiaomi_hyperos.name: Xiaomi Find Device
xiaomi_hyperos.reason: CRITICAL: Validated on boot by Xiaomi TrustZone keystore and lockscreen daemon. Disabling triggers continuous crash loops on restart.

xiaomi_hyperos.name: Xiaomi PowerKeeper
xiaomi_hyperos.reason: Controls display refresh rate switching (120Hz/90Hz/60Hz dynamic profiles) and thermal governors. Disabling caps display at 60Hz permanently and breaks battery health settings.

xiaomi_hyperos.name: Xiaomi Service Framework (XMSF)
xiaomi_hyperos.reason: Provides Xiaomi Cloud sync, Mi Push token distribution, and theme authentication. Removing breaks Xiaomi push notifications and account auth.

xiaomi_hyperos.name: POCO Launcher
xiaomi_hyperos.reason: Default home launcher and recent apps gesture provider for POCO devices. Disabling without a third-party launcher active renders device completely unnavigable.

xiaomi_hyperos.name: MIUI Home Launcher
xiaomi_hyperos.reason: Default launcher and gesture navigation handler on Xiaomi/Redmi HyperOS. Disabling breaks full-screen gestures and recent apps view.

xiaomi_hyperos.name: MIUI Carrier Overlay
xiaomi_hyperos.reason: SystemUI resource overlay for HyperOS status bar and SIM card indicators. Disabling triggers SystemUI NullPointer crashes.

xiaomi_hyperos.name: Security Guard Provider
xiaomi_hyperos.reason: Antivirus definitions engine bound directly to com.miui.securitycenter. Removing causes periodic Security Center exception dialogs.

xiaomi_hyperos.name: Security Center Additions
xiaomi_hyperos.reason: IPC bridge for Security Center app permissions and biometric authentication hooks.

xiaomi_hyperos.name: Xiaomi Account
xiaomi_hyperos.reason: Required for device activation after reboots, bootloader unlocking authorization, and SIM card verification.

xiaomi_hyperos.name: MIUI Core System Resources
xiaomi_hyperos.reason: Shared styles, drawables, and themes for all HyperOS system dialogs. Removing induces immediate crash loop.

samsung_oneui.name: One UI Home
samsung_oneui.reason: Default launcher and recent apps overview. Disabling without another launcher brick-locks the desktop.

samsung_oneui.name: Knox Core Container
samsung_oneui.reason: Knox hardware security subsystem. Disabling triggers hardware key attestation failure on boot.

samsung_oneui.name: Samsung In-Call UI
samsung_oneui.reason: Renders phone call screen on One UI. Disabling causes silent incoming calls with no way to answer.

samsung_oneui.name: Samsung Setup Wizard
samsung_oneui.reason: Handles initial setup and post-OTA configuration. Disabling before completion locks user out.

samsung_oneui.name: Samsung Biometrics Service
samsung_oneui.reason: Fingerprint and Face Unlock hardware daemon. Disabling bricks lockscreen authentication.

samsung_oneui.name: Samsung Pay Core Framework
samsung_oneui.reason: Tied into Knox key store. On older One UI builds, removing cause intermittent Knox security warnings.

samsung_oneui.name: Samsung Settings Receiver
samsung_oneui.reason: Broadcast receiver for One UI global settings updates. Disabling breaks quick settings toggles.

samsung_oneui.name: Samsung Keyboard
samsung_oneui.reason: Default Samsung keyboard. Never disable unless Gboard or another IME is set as default.

bbk_coloros.name: ColorOS Launcher
bbk_coloros.reason: Default home screen and recent apps gesture coordinator on Oppo/Realme/OnePlus ColorOS/OxygenOS.

bbk_coloros.name: ColorOS Security Center
bbk_coloros.reason: Core security manager and permission engine on BBK devices. Removing causes bootloop on reboot.

bbk_coloros.name: Oplus Battery Service
bbk_coloros.reason: Manages SuperVOOC fast charging curves and thermal limits. Removing drops charging speed and breaks battery stats.

bbk_coloros.name: Oplus Security Permission
bbk_coloros.reason: Handles USB debugging, app installation authorizations, and rootless ADB security.

bbk_coloros.name: ColorOS Wireless Settings
bbk_coloros.reason: Manages Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and cellular network preference handoffs.

bbk_coloros.name: Oplus Athena Process Manager
bbk_coloros.reason: Low-level memory and process manager. Disabling causes unstable process lifecycle and UI freezes.

google_pixel.name: Pixel Launcher
google_pixel.reason: Default home screen, recent apps and the At a Glance widget on Pixel. Disabling it without another launcher installed makes the device unnavigable.

google_pixel.name: Android System Intelligence
google_pixel.reason: Powers Now Playing, Live Caption, smart reply, live translation and screen attention. Disabling it breaks those features and can crash the launcher's smartspace.

google_pixel.name: Device Health Services
google_pixel.reason: Adaptive Battery predictions, battery run-time estimates and thermal profiles. Removing it degrades battery life reporting and can break power management.

google_pixel.name: Google Phone
google_pixel.reason: The actual dialer UI on Pixel. Disabling it removes incoming-call screens and emergency dialling.

google_pixel.name: Settings Intelligence (Google)
google_pixel.reason: Settings search index and suggestion provider on Pixel. Disabling it leaves Settings search empty and breaks some quick-setting flows.

patterns.reason: Play Services modules (auth, location, ML, cast). They ship as separate packages and any one of them being disabled breaks Play Services for every app.
Google Services Framework variants. Removing them breaks Google account authentication.
Resource overlays applied to SystemUI and framework packages. Disabling one produces resource-not-found crashes in the status bar and lockscreen.
HyperOS/MIUI resource overlays for system UI. Same failure mode as above.
Knox security stack. Disabling a subunit invalidates hardware key attestation on the next boot.
Framework, APEX and extension packages (android.ext.shared, android.apex.*). Never a bloatware candidate.
